scope: Existing package scripts discovered by VS Code; review and real task execution, not an AI or complete-application quality assessment

checks: Package scripts: built-in npm task discovery includes ungrouped check, displays actual script and pre/post declarations, excludes dev/watch/install/publish, never executes while listing and rejects a changed manifest before launch

Package scripts: actual npm command passes, model-free source edit makes the original assertion fail, native undo restores pass and exact source; declared npm hooks run according to npm success/failure semantics

setupFailures.cause: npm absent from the test process PATH
setupFailures.resolution: Prepared npm in ignored local test storage and added its shim directory to the test process PATH; same product and test assertions then passed.

setupFailures.cause: First package-manager command targeted a directory that had not yet been created
setupFailures.resolution: Created the owned test directory. Package manager temporarily updated the workspace lockfile with a test-only importer; restored that exact setup-only lockfile change. No product dependency added.

limitations: Task names do not prove correctness or one-shot behavior. Users must review the actual command and scripts.
Only exact npm-provider script names test/build/check/typecheck/lint are included. Other commands can use explicit process/shell tasks.
The built-in task provider, local package manager and project dependencies must already be available.
No test-count extraction, full-project snapshot, optimization measurement, scientific or model-quality verdict is provided.
